summary.text: A man in his 70s with high-risk localized prostate adenocarcinoma (Gleason 4 + 3 = 7, clinical stage cT1cN0M0, stage IIIA) and a rising PSA completed staging and a baseline IPSS of 4. He then underwent definitive IMRT with a simultaneous integrated boost to the prostate and pelvic lymph nodes with concurrent leuprolide, and all planning dose constraints were met.

Eight days after completion of radiotherapy he developed acute urinary retention with overflow incontinence, constipation and post-renal acute kidney injury with creatinine 4.89 mg/dL. He was hospitalized and a Foley catheter was placed with an initial urine output of about 1 liter, and creatinine improved to 1.46 mg/dL after decompression.

CT showed moderate left perinephric and periureteric stranding with mild hydronephrosis and no obstructing calculus, and renal ultrasound showed bilateral chronic renal disease changes without gross hydronephrosis, supporting recent post-renal obstruction. He received tamsulosin, a polyethylene glycol bowel regimen and supportive care without surgical decompression, and was discharged with the Foley catheter in place.

At one month his bowel movements had normalized and the catheter remained in place pending urology follow-up. Because of continued retention symptoms he underwent TURP two months after radiation therapy, and the Foley catheter was removed about five days later with normal voiding.
